title: The band, the ceiling and the wiring
intro: The level above gives the boundaries, the capacity number and the broadcast results. This level gives the instruments that produced them: how the band was first drawn before any of the four statistics were computed, what the sweep at its onset substitutes into the model, what the count of 25 is a count of, and what each broadcast measurement is scored against.

chapters.title: Drawing the boundaries
chapters.body:
The layer numbers need reading first. The paper records 25 evenly spaced layers of the [[residual-stream]] and reindexes them onto a 0 to 100 scale ([[layer-percentage-indexing]]). L38 is therefore a point 38 percent of the way through the depth, not the thirty-eighth layer, and the same numbers can be quoted across models of different sizes.

The first cut at the boundaries uses none of the four statistics. For every pair of layers, the paper compares the geometry of the lens vectors by centered kernel alignment: each layer contributes its matrix of pairwise similarities among its own lens vectors, and the two matrices are compared ([[cka]]). The resulting layer-by-layer matrix falls into three blocks — an early block covering roughly the first third, a long middle block, and a small late block ([[fig-27]]).

Blocks alone do not say which block is the workspace. Two anchors settle it, neither of which has to be measured. The final layer's lens vectors must encode next-token predictions, because little else is left for them to encode. The first layer's cannot mean much, because the first layer can only encode the identity of the token sitting at that position. The middle block is what remains, and the three regions take the names [[sensory-layers]], [[workspace-layers]] and [[motor-layers]].

Two hedges travel with the picture. The analyses run on subsampled layers, which makes the block edges look sharper than they are, and in some models the transition is gradual and contains sub-blocks ([[layer-subsampling]]).

The four statistics that refine the boundaries ([[workspace-boundary-metrics]], [[fig-28]]) are all read through the same instrument. So the empty early band may be a failure of the lens at those depths rather than a fact about the model ([[early-layer-lens-degeneracy]]).
chapters.childScope: Take the four boundary statistics one at a time — [[lens-next-token-accuracy]], [[readout-excess-kurtosis]], [[top1-autocorrelation]] against its [[position-shuffled-null]], and [[j-space-effective-dimensionality]] — saying what each quantity measures, why each marks the boundary it marks, and why dimensionality rises a second time at the motor transition as [[jacobian-approaches-identity]] and the readout collapses toward the plain [[unembedding-matrix]] ([[fig-28]]).

chapters.title: One test the lens does not run
chapters.body:
The construction is a substitution at the input. A concept token's input embedding is replaced with the blend $(1-\alpha)\, e_B + \alpha\, e_A$ of two country embeddings, inside ordinary carrier sentences such as "My sister has always wanted to visit ___" ([[embedding-mixture-experiment]]). Sixteen pairs of single-token country names are crossed with forty carrier sentences. For each trial $\alpha$ is swept from 0 to 1, and the residual stream at the mixed token's position is recorded at every layer.

The measurement that follows uses no lens at all. For each trial and each layer, the activation is projected onto the line joining that trial's pure-$B$ activation at $\alpha = 0$ to its pure-$A$ activation at $\alpha = 1$, at the same position and layer. That share is 0 at one end of the sweep and 1 at the other by construction, so the sweep only asks what happens in between. Early layers give a smooth ramp. From about L38 the activation instead sits near one endpoint or the other and jumps between them at a threshold value of $\alpha$ ([[fig-29]]).

The sharpness is then quantified as [[transition-width]]: the change in $\alpha$ needed to move the share from 10 percent to 90 percent. It falls steeply over roughly layers 21 to 42. Measured separately, the activation's component along the two concepts' lens vectors sharpens earlier and further than its complement, which is obtained by projecting the top sixteen lens vectors out ([[j-space-component]], [[fig-70]]).

An average could hide the effect entirely. At the most ambiguous $\alpha$, individual trials do not sit at 0.5: by mid-depth the J-space component's distribution is bimodal near 0 and near 1, while the non-J-space component still carries mass in the middle ([[bimodal-commitment]], [[fig-71]]).

The paper reads this as the analog of [[ignition]]. The input, though, is an embedding blend the model never receives in ordinary text.

chapters.title: What the count of 25 is a count of
chapters.body:
Occupancy is the output of a stopping rule rather than a direct reading. At each position and layer, the paper solves for the sparse nonnegative combination of $K$ lens vectors that best reconstructs the activation ([[sparse-decomposition]]), using gradient pursuit, a greedy sparse-approximation algorithm ([[gradient-pursuit]]). $K$ is raised until the marginal improvement in reconstruction from one more lens vector falls below the improvement offered by a control set of random directions of the same size. The value of $K$ at that crossing is the [[j-space-occupancy]]: near zero through the first third of the layers, and about 25 in the median case across the band, with the value varying by context ([[fig-30]]).

What those vectors account for is separately small. With $K$ set to the median occupancy at each workspace layer, the variance they explain above a same-size random control never exceeds 10 percent ([[excess-variance-explained]]). The activations are dominated by information outside the workspace.

A second decomposition agrees. Only a small share of [[sparse-autoencoder]] features have decoder directions that project sharply through the lens ([[lens-kurtosis]]), and the features that do not are dominated by low-level syntactic and bookkeeping directions ([[bookkeeping-features]]).

One caveat limits what the number means. Occupancy counts lens vectors active above chance, not ideas, and several vectors may stand together for one broader concept ([[vectors-versus-concepts]]).

The formal definition carries the same free parameter. The lens vectors span the whole residual stream, so the J-space is not a subspace at all; fixed at a sparsity level $k$, it is the union of the cones of nonnegative combinations of any $k$ of them ([[eq-jspace-cones]], [[union-of-cones]]). The paper sets $k$ by hand, using values between 10 and 25 for two different purposes ([[sparsity-level-k]]).

chapters.title: Six words at a time, or a whole family
chapters.body:
Presence in the readout is scored by a rule worth stating. The model reads 80-word comma-separated lists, and at each comma a word counts as present if its best rank across the workspace layers L38 to L92 falls in the top 25 ([[word-list-experiment]], [[band-min-rank]]). The cutoff is checked rather than assumed: the count of already-read words is plotted against the threshold $K$, alongside control words that never appear in the prompt ([[rank-threshold-robustness]], [[fig-31]]).

Pooling across layers is doing part of the work. Repeating the measurement at the single workspace layer L79 leaves the qualitative picture unchanged but drops the unrelated-word count from about six to one or two ([[single-layer-capacity]], [[fig-72]]). The band holds six because different concepts sit at different depths ([[unrelated-list-capacity]]).

The related-word case is visible from the first item. After the single word "shark", the readout already contains "whale," "fish," "swimming," "submarine," "ocean" — almost none of which have been read ([[category-loading]]).

What clears the workspace is not elapsed time. Eight animals followed by color words leaves the readout dominated by colors after a single color has been presented, and lists built from four consecutive 20-word category blocks show each category entering at its own block and clearing within a few words of the switch ([[category-displacement]]). Within a block, individual words persist long after they are read.

Two further limits sit around the number. The capacity is per token position, and attention can still fetch content from earlier positions ([[per-position-capacity]]). And when the model is told to hold two things at once, two static concepts share tokens at the control rate, 0.46 against 0.53, whereas a concept and a running arithmetic problem almost never share a token, 0.09 against 0.29 ([[workspace-competition]], [[co-occupancy]]).

chapters.title: What the broadcast numbers are compared against
chapters.body:
The claim rests on two directions of travel through the network. Content written into the residual stream at a position is visible to every later layer at that position, and attention makes a position's content available to later positions ([[j-space-broadcast]]).

Depth is measured by gain. For a unit direction $v$ at layer $\ell$, the [[mlp-gain]] is the output norm of the [[mlp-block]] at layer $\ell+1$ applied to $v$, divided by the median output norm over isotropic random directions, so that a random direction scores 1 by construction ([[fig-32]]). The paper flags what the measurement leaves out: the block is applied to the direction on its own, which is never how it is used in practice ([[mlp-gain-context-caveat]]).

The comparison is what carries the result. Sorting sparse autoencoder decoder directions into six equal bins by lens kurtosis gives a graded control rather than a binary one, and gain rises monotonically across the bins ([[kappa-strata]]). In the early workspace layers the top bin outscores the lens vectors themselves, which the paper takes as evidence that the lens captures only part of the workspace it is estimating.

Across positions the test is on the [[ov-circuit]], the value-then-output map of a head. Gain is one criterion. Label preservation is the other: the mean reciprocal rank of $\cos(W_{OV} v_i, v_i)$ among that head's cosines with the other directions in the population, referenced to random so that a head copying everything indiscriminately scores zero ([[median-reciprocal-rank]]). Heads are ranked on each criterion, scored by their worse rank, and the best 1 percent are kept ([[broadcast-head-selection-rule]], [[fig-33]]).

The controls are shaped to match. One is the lens vectors under a single fixed random rotation, which preserves their spectrum and pairwise geometry while destroying their alignment with the weights ([[j-rotated-control]]). The selected heads concentrate in the first half of the band, where the lens vectors span the fewest dimensions and one OV map can therefore carry a larger share of them ([[broadcast-head-layer-placement]]).
chapters.childScope: Cover the weight-level broadcast evidence in full: [[neuron-connectivity]] breadth and [[tail-energy]] strength against individual MLP neurons, with the [[read-write-asymmetry]] between early and late workspace layers ([[fig-76]], [[fig-77]], [[fig-78]]); the [[composition-score]] against attention weights and its [[value-vs-query-key-asymmetry]] ([[fig-79]]); and what ablating the [[broadcast-heads]] does and does not disturb, readout recall against behaviour ([[fig-34]]).
